summary: GPU memory pressure and output anomalies after aggressive prefetch + quant profile: safe unwind + dry-run playbook
description: Issue summary: After applying an aggressive optimizer profile that enabled aggressive prefix prefetch and switched the model to the 8-bit quant variant, BrightPost Health began seeing increased GPU memory pressure, intermittent 5xx stream disconnects, and occasional token-level degradation (repeated tokens and truncation artifacts) for long-lived streaming sessions. Impact: ~5% of live requests experienced disconnects; 95th latency rose from ~220ms to ~900ms for the affected endpoints; two dedicated nodes reported transient GPU OOMs and were automatically rebooted. Environment: Dedicated pool (tenant: brightpost-prod), model pin: redwood/gpt-medium-quant8, optimizer profile applied: aggressive-prefetch-v3, dynamic batching config: max_batch_tokens=2048, kv_cache_eviction_threshold default. Timeline: 2026-03-12 03:10 UTC - profile rolled to 100% for tenant; 03:24 UTC - first 5xxs; 03:40 UTC - automated node reboot triggered; 04:00 UTC - customer reported production impact. Current behavior: persistent memory growth across long sessions and symptom set described above. Expected behavior: stable memory footprint with graceful eviction, no output artifacts, and latency within SLOs. This ticket requests stepwise guidance to safely unwind the optimizer changes, a dry-run checklist to validate fixes without full rollback, and a short-term mitigation to restore customer throughput while preserving logs for postmortem.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the tenant's dedicated pool and pin model to redwood/gpt-medium-quant8
2) Apply optimizer profile aggressive-prefetch-v3 (enables prefix prefetch and increases prefetch window to 4k tokens),
3) Start long-lived streaming sessions with repeated conversational prefixes > 3k tokens and high concurrency (simulate 40 parallel streams),
4) Configure dynamic batching with max_batch_tokens=2048 and ephemeral burst to 4096,
5) Observe GPU memory over 90% within ~10-20 minutes and stream disconnects / 5xxs in logs.

2026-03-12 04:22 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Observed KV cache growth correlating with prefix prefetch window increase. Possible mismatch between quant variant working set and eviction heuristics.

2026-03-12 05:24 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Proposed staged dry-run: 1) enable per-tenant prefetched_kv_eviction_threshold=0.65, 2) lower max_batch_tokens to 512 for 10% traffic, 3) divert 5% traffic to stable model redwood/gpt-medium (no quant).
investigation_notes: KV cache growth is strongly correlated to session length and prefix prefetch window; eviction runs were late due to large continuous-batch coalescing and delayed async eviction tasks.
Quant8 variant has slightly larger on-device working set because of runtime layout differences; combined with aggressive batching this pushed memory over threshold in some nodes.
No evidence of model corruption; token artifacts likely due to truncated KV entries when eviction occurred during in-flight autoregressive generation.
Node-level heap traces point to delayed GC of ephemeral buffers during batch coalescing; scheduler metrics show large 'coalesced_batch_size' spikes at peak times.
proposed_action_plan: - Apply per-tenant emergency settings: prefetched_kv_eviction_threshold=0.65 and enable aggressive_kv_eviction=true for brightpost-prod.
- Lower tenant dynamic batching: set max_batch_tokens=512 and max_concurrent_streams=20 for 10 minutes to avoid further OOMs.
- Open traffic split: route 5% of traffic to redwood/gpt-medium (stable FP variant) using traffic-split API to validate behavioral parity.
- Run synthetic long-session load at production QPS directed at 5% canary to measure latency/outputs and validate no truncation artifacts.
- Monitor GPU memory, kv_cache_entries, coalesced_batch_size, and repeated-token-detector alerts in Grafana dashboards.
- Gradually expand traffic to 25% canary over 15 minutes, keep eviction thresholds and batching conservative,
- If stable, perform tenant-level deactivation of aggressive-prefetch-v3 (roll back optimizer flags) and rehydrate per-tenant snapshot to pre-change optimizer profile.
- Once confirmed, restore max_batch_tokens incrementally back to previous values with 10-minute holdpoints.
resolution_summary: 2026-03-13 09:35 - Applied emergency eviction threshold and reduced batching; spun up 5% canary on stable FP model. Metrics normalized (GPU memory P95 dropped below 60%, 5xx rate returned to baseline). Customer confirmed reduced client-side disconnects. Plan for controlled unwind and automation improvements created; awaiting customer signoff to fully remove aggressive-prefetch-v3.
workarounds: Enable emergency eviction threshold prefetched_kv_eviction_threshold=0.65 (tenant-level override),
Temporarily pin traffic fraction to stable non-quant model with traffic-split API (5-25%),
Lower dynamic batching tokens: max_batch_tokens=512 and reduce burst capacity
If OOMs persist, schedule node drain of affected instance and reallocate to a node with larger GPU memory (manual)
